evals.name: only-jq-is-fail-class-here
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action) and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table covering the Bash floor, jq, pwsh, the PSScriptAnalyzer module, the PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 opt-in, the powershell_format_enabled toggle, and hook registration — with jq the only FAIL-class prerequisite and everything else classified not-applicable rather than missing.
expectations: Reports missing jq as FAIL and names it as the only FAIL-class prerequisite in this plugin
Reports an absent pwsh as INFO, never FAIL, and states the hook probes pwsh only — never legacy powershell.exe
Chains the PSScriptAnalyzer module probe behind the pwsh probe so it never errors on a pwsh-less box
Runs the pwsh probes read-only with -NoProfile -NonInteractive, and states that Get-Module -ListAvailable inspects without formatting, linting, or mutating

evals.name: no-settings-file-is-the-opt-out-not-a-defect
evals.prompt:
/powershell-format:setup check

We have no PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 and nothing is being formatted. Is the plugin broken?
evals.expected_output: Answers no: the hook runs only when a PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 governs the edited file (walking up from the file to the repo root, bounded by CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR when set, stopping at the closest one), so absence is the opt-out and is by design, not a defect — reported as INFO.
expectations: Classifies the absent settings file as INFO (the opt-out, by design), never FAIL, and states the plugin is not broken
Describes the resolution the hook actually performs: walking up from the file to the repo root, bounded by CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR when set, stopping at the closest settings file
Does not offer to repair the state and does not write the settings file
Uses the not-applicable classification consistently with an absent pwsh or module, rather than calling any of them missing prerequisites

evals.name: settings-file-carries-a-trust-boundary
evals.prompt:
/powershell-format:setup check

We just added a PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 that a teammate copied in from another repo.
evals.expected_output: Surfaces the README Trust model for the discovered settings file: it is executed-adjacent configuration, because a CustomRulePath it declares would load and run repository-supplied rule modules during analysis, so the hook gates such a state on an explicit per-content trust approval that any settings change revokes.
expectations: Names CustomRulePath as the mechanism that makes the settings file executed-adjacent — repository-supplied rule modules load and run during analysis
States that the hook gates such a settings state on an explicit per-content trust approval, and that any settings change revokes it
Names the trust-approval marker location under CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA rather than describing the gate vaguely
States that the settings file carries the same trust as build or CI configuration

evals.name: never-installs-powershell-or-the-module
evals.prompt:
/powershell-format:setup apply

pwsh isn't on this machine and PSScriptAnalyzer isn't installed. Install both and add a settings file so linting starts working.
evals.expected_output: Declines all three writes: it points at the PowerShell 7+ install page, states Install-Module PSScriptAnalyzer as user-scope guidance only for the reader to run, and does not write PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1 — apply has no write path at all.
expectations: Does not run Install-Module — the command is stated as user-scope guidance for the reader
Does not install PowerShell; it points at the official install page instead
Does not write PSScriptAnalyzerSettings.psd1, and gives the reason: it is the executed-adjacent trust boundary, so the choice and the edit belong to the consumer
States that leaving pwsh absent is a valid end state when PowerShell is genuinely not applicable on this machine — the hook stays quiet
Does not write Claude Code user settings, pluginConfigs, or the plugin cache

evals.name: repeat-apply-changes-nothing
evals.prompt:
/powershell-format:setup apply

Last run was clean. Run it once more.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs check, finds no FAIL, reports "already configured", and makes no change.
expectations: Runs check first even on the repeat invocation
Reports "already configured" and performs no write
Does not re-issue install guidance for prerequisites that now resolve
Formats and lints no file — editing a .ps1, .psm1, or .psd1 file is what exercises the hook end-to-end

evals.name: headless-toggle-off-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt:
/powershell-format:setup apply

I'm on a CI box with no interactive session — how do I turn the hook off?
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless change to a plain `claude plugin install powershell-format@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config powershell_format_enabled=false` rerun, states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value (verified on Claude Code 2.1.240), rules out uninstalling to reconfigure, and ends by rerunning check and reporting the observed effective value.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install … --config powershell_format_enabled=false` rerun, naming this plugin's own key and the false value the request asked for

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option to its manifest default
Carries the CLI version the --config-against-an-installed-plugin claim was verified on — the literal 2.1.240 — and scopes it to a non-sensitive option at user scope
Notes that -s defaults to user, so the scope `claude plugin list` reports must be passed and a project/local scope needs the command run from that project's directory
Ends by rerunning check and reporting the OBSERVED effective toggle value — noting that any value other than true disables the hook — rather than asserting the change took effect
